score: COMPOSER: the CINEMATIC score for this film

Design the music for this 59.5 s film. The OWNER'S NOTE: the current score (intimate felt piano + solo cello) is too small for this serious topic; it should be CINEMATIC, and the film now looks like a bold graphic comic book. A promise spoken 700 years early and kept. Give it real cinematic scale: a full string section, low brass or horns, deep percussion (big low drums / timpani) used sparingly at the turns, and one huge but reverent swell. Keep ONE simple hummable 'promise tune' (heard unfinished at the promise ~12-14 s, still unfinished at the birth ~23 s 'God's promise came true', and finally completed only in the last hold after 'He came to us.'). The music must still sit UNDER the narration and drop nearly out under the two short KJV lines (~16.0-17.4 and ~33.8-36.3), go to TRUE silence in the 1 s pause (~38.0-39.0), come back with drive on 'The wise men went' (~42.1), go sacred and still for heaven / cross / tomb (~47-52, no drums), swell on 'He rose from the dead' (~52.7-53.8), drop out under 'He came to us.' (~55.2-56.4), and finish the tune in the 3 s hold. No choir with words, no trailer 'braaam', no cheesy Middle-East scales, no rock drums. Grace, not fear.
